findings.note: Right size: one decision record and a rename while there are zero users. Everything else (presence, decay, fuses, latency) is denominated in watches, so this unblocks them. Keep a sub-watch fractional beat available so talking can cost the world time (S1-R3) without a second unit; see S2-10.

findings.amended: Add actor/cause to every WorldEffect and a minimal Act record {actorId, verb, objectRef, motiveTag, spaceId, watch, perceptibility} written by behavior commits. Defer full preconditions/considerations utility selection until a thread needs NPCs choosing behaviors; the Act log is the spine, the behavior-selection rewrite is not.
findings.note: This is the single most important rec for P4: inference trails are renderings of Acts to observers (cf. Dwarf Fortress event logs, Versu/Prom Week social-exchange records, Talk of the Town). Gold-plating risk is bundling the BehaviorModule commit/selection rewrite with it; separate them. Perceptibility should be data per verb, not a boolean.

findings.amended: Adopt Fact / Claim / Belief {holder, claimId, confidence, source kind, learnedWatch, hops}, and let a Claim mutate in fidelity as it hops (Talk of the Town style) so rumour degradation and rival spoofing are the same mechanism. Player notebook is the player's Belief set; NPC text reads only the speaker's Beliefs.
findings.note: Without this, generation grounding (S2-06), notebook (S2-12), Reports (S2-09) and diffusion (S2-10) have no shared substrate. Under-reach in the original: no mention of fidelity decay or mutation, which is what makes gossip a mystery rather than a database. Keep confidence coarse (3-4 bands) so it can be voiced qualitatively in speech, per the rejected CK3 numeric odds.

Directly implements P2 and keeps generated text a view, never state, which protects determinism and P1. TextSourcePort (authored|pool|generated) is the right seam. Freezing shown text into ConversationHistory is the same trick Hades/Inkle use for continuity. Retiring 08 as written is correct; the replacement change should be named for text generation plus authoring kit, not intent parsing.

findings.amended: Treat runtime SLM generation as a first-class tier, not a late optional one: run a timing spike on the real Mac now, then decide which text classes (Tier-2 lines, ambient, letters, gazette) are runtime-generated and seed-cached into the save versus pool-baked. Authoring-time drafting by a larger model stays as the quality floor and the source of few-shot exemplars.
findings.note: P2 says a large share of text comes from local small models; as drafted this rec leans toward making that share mostly baked content, which under-serves P2. The determinism worry is real but is solved by freezing output into the save (S2-04), not by avoiding runtime generation. Reference: Generative Agents memory-retrieval grounding, AI Dungeon-style caching is not wanted; Façade-style templated slots are the safe fallback.

LineBrief plus a pure gate is the anti-slop bar made executable and runs at both authoring and runtime, which fits the eval runner. Retry once then fall back to a pool line is the right failure shape for a player-facing system. Add the grounding tier as the hard gate (never states a fact outside the speaker's Beliefs); style tiers can be soft. Depends on S2-03.

Rival tells as a reading puzzle is a strong P4 payoff (cf. Papers Please discrepancy-spotting, Obra Dinn corroboration). Deterministic post-pass guarantees reliability regardless of model behaviour. Not needed until a rival thread exists; just reserve tellProfile on the schema when rivals are next touched. Beware of tells being so uniform they become a checklist: allow per-rival partial tells.

This is the collaborative-enrichment workflow of P1 and P2 made concrete, and fixing the hand/pool/templated split prevents incompatible first content. The draft/accept CLI is the highest-value piece since the owner wants help authoring. Include a Tier-1 'voice register' card per character, matching the existing note that register is diction and cadence, not performed voice.

findings.amended: Define Report {actId, channelId, latencyWatches, reliability, spoofSignature?} as the only path by which a remote Act becomes a player Belief (S2-03). Give rivals a small hidden agenda emitting Acts, and add the invariant eval, but let the threshold and N be per-thread data so some Acts are deliberately slow or only reconstructable.
findings.note: Operationalises the owner's 'aware of that interaction at some point' rule and is testable. Risk: a strict every-heavy-Act-yields-Report-within-N invariant could flatten P4 into guaranteed notification; the Report may be a trace (a gap, a price move), not a message. Merge design with S2-02 and S2-03 so Report is a Belief delivery, not a fourth channel.

findings.amended: Split embodied reactive cascades (keep hop cap) from closed-form information diffusion per watch over the Belief graph. Instead of wall-clock storyteller release, give reading, conversing and waiting a small fractional-watch cost so the world advances with player activity and pause stays a true freeze.
findings.note: The diagnosis is right and the split is the correct technique (cf. Dwarf Fortress off-screen simulation, Crusader Kings tick-based rumour spread). Wall-clock beats are wrong here: they punish careful reading, break the pause-freezes-room rule, and undercut determinism; S1-R3 already says the cost of talking comes from the world, which the fractional-watch cost delivers.

Pure (entity, watch, seed) -> placement is the Ultima VII / Skyrim schedule pattern and gives deterministic, testable presence. Starting entities off-stage and a defined catch-up on jump are exactly the gaps that would otherwise produce visible popping. Catch-up should emit Acts via S2-02, so land that first.

findings.amended: Fix the notebook categories now as a Belief-view (known, suspected, partial, omitted-with-referent) and defer richer features (staleness, contradiction pairs, who-else-knows, graded hypotheses, spoof flags) to the notebook UI work, adding them one at a time as threads use them.
findings.note: The referent rule for omissions is the key insight and honours the owner's gaps category without leaking. Obra Dinn corroboration grading is the right reference for hypotheses. The original is a feature list that should not be spec'd in one go; categories must be derivable from S2-03 Belief fields so the notebook is a view, not a second store.

Hubs before leaves is the correct build order and fits P1. Largely subsumed by S2-01, S2-02, S2-03 and S2-16, so treat it as the sequencing statement for those rather than separate work. Including a player resource ledger here is under-reached elsewhere and belongs in the hub list explicitly.

Small, data-driven refactor that directly serves P1 and epoch-skinnability (a Cold War pack should not inherit feudal coin physics). Do it before more instrument modes exist. Include scar as optional so non-scarring modes stay clean.

findings.amended: Write the 4-6 loops as one table with a tuning key each, and make discovery a decaying evidence score per observer with thresholds, while keeping decay rates slow and uneven so the player never reads it as a clean timer. Forged fiat should raise evidence sharply but not jump straight to 'attributed'.
findings.note: Loops table is the right design artefact (cf. stealth heat decay in Hitman and GTA wanted levels, Frostpunk's discontent). Without a balancing side the first forgery is a death sentence, which defeats exploration. P4 caveat: decay must itself be inferable via world traces, not a visible meter. Compatible with S2-18 if the evidence score is keyed per observer.

findings.amended: Add bearsOnThreadId and supportedBy {entityId | institutionalLineageId} to pillars, derive thread inertia from live pillar weights, and treat the Leverage Chain as a derived query. Surface chains to the player only indirectly (advisor remarks, notebook referents), with weaken_support as the verb.
findings.note: S1-R1 requires a Leverage Chain definition in the spine and this is the only concrete one offered; reference is Crusader Kings faction support graphs and Disco Elysium-style indirect pressure points. Under-reach: no statement of how the player discovers the chain, which is the actual gameplay. Derived rather than stored inertia avoids a second source of truth.

findings.amended: Adopt the eight rules as a one-paragraph-each index in DESIGN_NOTES, each pointing to the recommendation that fleshes it out (S2-01, 02, 16, 15, 19, 18, 13) and the code it constrains; do not write full specs up front.
findings.note: Matches the owner's S1-R1 position: minimal spine, not everything up front. As written it duplicates other recs, so it is an index rather than new work. Add 'validation by rejection, never throwing' as an explicit engine convention since it affects every future reducer.

findings.amended: Make illicit insertion spend Delta and require zenith (rejecting rather than throwing otherwise), and give each pressure stock diegetic tells in the world. Fold the observer-keyed discovery into the per-observer evidence score of S2-15 rather than a separate change.
findings.note: A zenith window for risky insertion creates a real timing decision (cf. Kerbal Space Program launch windows) and ties orbital play to economy. Stock tells are strong P4 material. Avoid inventing a new discovery structure; one evidence model serves both recs.

findings.amended: Decide that one emergency is dominant at a time with others queued (simple, readable), add EmergencyRuntime {id, startedAtWatch, fuseRemainingWatches, scope}, and make compounding scope-aware with rate from the blueprint. Communicate the fuse indirectly through NPC behaviour and advisor unease, not a countdown.
findings.note: Fuse-based crises are a proven tension source (cf. Frostpunk, CK3 crisis events). The current uniform compounding is a bug in design terms and should be fixed whenever emergencies next get content. Cardinality decision should be written in the S2-17 index now even though implementation can wait.

overall: Start with the foundations the whole spine hangs on: S2-01 (clock), S2-02 (actor-tagged effects and the Act record, without the behavior-selection rewrite), S2-03 (Fact/Claim/Belief) and S2-13/S2-17 as the sequencing index, plus S2-16 because S1-R1 needs a Leverage Chain definition. Then, before 06, do the information-flow trio S2-09 (Report), S2-10 (diffusion with a fractional-watch cost, not wall-clock beats) and S2-11 (presence), which together implement the owner's 'aware at some point' rule and P4. Next settle the text pipeline: S2-04 immediately as a rule, then a real-Mac timing spike so S2-05 can commit to a runtime SLM tier that honours P2 rather than defaulting to baked content, with S2-08 (authoring kit) and S2-06 (LineBrief and gate) built on the Belief model. In parallel, S2-14, S2-15 and S2-18 rework economy and discovery into one data-driven per-observer evidence model with real balancing loops. Leave S2-07 (rival tells), S2-12 (notebook feature set beyond the categories) and S2-19 (emergency fuses) until their content exists, writing only their cardinality and schema reservations into the spine now.
